suggested_titles.academic: Jurisdictional Proof of God: The Resurrection as a Legal Exception to Death's Claim
suggested_titles.provocative: The One Death Could Not Hold: Why Resurrection Proves God

opening_analysis.diagnosis: The opening is strong: a bold, paradoxical claim immediately grabs attention. The thesis is visible in the first sentence. The problem (how to prove God) is implied but not explicitly stated until later. The opening could benefit from a brief framing of why this matters or what it challenges.

flow.suggested_reorder: No reordering needed; the flow is logical and builds well.

paragraph_function_map.main_point: God can be proved only by a rightful exception to the deepest rule.
Every created thing is under law.
Matter, bodies, minds, moral agents, and living things are all under specific laws.
Merely breaking a rule does not prove God.
A demon, magician, simulator, or advanced intelligence could break a rule.
Raw exception is not enough; the exception must be rightful.
Rightful exception means the Law recognizing its own Author.
God is proven when the deepest law encounters someone it cannot lawfully bind.
Sin gives death jurisdiction; death has legal ground only over the guilty.
Death can hold the guilty, corruptible, and broken, but not the one who owes it nothing.
The proof is not that Jesus came back, but that death had no jurisdiction over Him.
A non-arbitrary exception that fulfills justice, not violates it.
If one person passes through the deepest constraint without being owned, He is its rightful superior.
Rightful authority proves God, not mere power.
Power could be evil, alien, technological, or deceptive; rightful authority is different.
If someone enters death innocently and death cannot keep Him, it is justice, not force.
This proves moral authority over the final law.
God is proven when the final law is forced to confess one man is above it.
Death is the final law; Christ enters, death finds no claim, death loses.
A true proof is the deepest rule meeting the one it had no right to bind.

rearrangement_suggestions: No rearrangement needed; the structure is logical and effective.
top_3_fixes: Improve the title to be more descriptive and searchable, e.g., 'Proof by Jurisdiction: The Resurrection as a Rightful Exception'.
Add an explicit statement of the problem in the first paragraph to orient the reader more clearly.
Consider adding a brief summary or transition at the end of the opening section to reinforce the thesis before moving into the proof.
